title: Sharing keys safely
syllabusUnit: Unit III: Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange & ElGamal
covers: Diffie-Hellman, ElGamal, key distribution & management, MITM
learningGoals: You will be able to illustrate the Diffie-Hellman key exchange using the paint-mixing analogy.
You will be able to calculate a shared secret from public and private keys.
You will be able to explain how a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks unauthenticated Diffie-Hellman.

lessonCards.title: Diffie-Hellman Paint Mixing
lessonCards.analogy: Alice and Bob start with common yellow paint. Each adds a secret color, swaps the mix, and adds their secret again to get matching brown.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Alice picks private a, publishes A = g^a mod p. Bob picks private b, publishes B = g^b mod p. Alice computes B^a mod p; Bob computes A^b mod p. Both get g^(ab) mod p!
lessonCards.example: An eavesdropper sees g, p, A, and B, but cannot calculate g^(ab) without solving the discrete log problem.

lessonCards.title: The Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) Threat
lessonCards.analogy: An imposter intercepting letters at the post office, creating separate secret codes with Alice and Bob.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Unauthenticated Diffie-Hellman is vulnerable to MITM: Mallory intercepts Alice's A and sends her M1; intercepts Bob's B and sends him M2. She decrypts and re-encrypts all traffic.
lessonCards.example: Solution: Authenticate public keys using digital signatures and X.509 certificates.

lessonCards.title: The ElGamal Cryptosystem
lessonCards.analogy: Extending Diffie-Hellman into a complete public-key encryption and digital signature system.
lessonCards.coreConcept: Published by Taher ElGamal in 1985: uses DLP over cyclic groups. Encryption produces two ciphertext parts (c1, c2) using an ephemeral random session key.
lessonCards.example: ElGamal is randomized: encrypting the identical message twice produces totally different ciphertexts.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of the Diffie-Hellman protocol?
options: To enable two parties to agree on a shared secret key across an insecure public channel
To scan networks for open ports
questions.explanation: Whitfield Diffie and Martin Hellman designed this protocol in 1976 to solve the ancient problem of key distribution over insecure networks.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Diffie-Hellman securely derives shared symmetric keys across the public internet.
It does not compress files.
Hashing is performed by SHA-256.
Port scanning is network enumeration.
questions.realWorldExample: Diffie-Hellman was the first published public-key cryptographic protocol.

questions.prompt: In Diffie-Hellman with modulus p = 23 and generator g = 5, Alice chooses private key a = 6. What is her public key A = g^a mod p?
wrongExplanations: Correct! 5^6 mod 23 = 8.
15 is incorrect.
2 is incorrect.
6 is Alice's private key.
questions.realWorldExample: Alice sends public key A = 8 openly across the internet to Bob.

questions.prompt: Why is standard anonymous Diffie-Hellman vulnerable to a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack?
options: It provides no authentication of the participants' identities
questions.explanation: Because public values A and B are unauthenticated, an attacker can substitute their own public keys and establish independent keys with both parties.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Without digital signatures or certificates, neither party can verify who they are talking to.
Prime numbers are mathematically required.
Diffie-Hellman works over any network medium.
Exponents in real systems are hundreds of bits.
questions.realWorldExample: TLS 1.3 uses Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman (ECDHE) signed by certificate authorities to prevent MITM.

questions.prompt: What makes Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman (DHE / ECDHE) provide 'Forward Secrecy'?
options: A fresh private key is generated for every session and erased from memory immediately after
It uses keys that last 100 years
It saves all master keys on the hard drive
questions.explanation: If a server's long-term certificate private key is stolen years later, past recorded traffic cannot be decrypted because session keys were erased.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Forward Secrecy ensures past sessions remain secure even after future key compromise.
Persistent keys destroy forward secrecy.
Saving keys to disk enables retrospective decryption.
Radio transmission has no security advantage.
questions.realWorldExample: Modern browsers flag websites that do not support Forward Secrecy as legacy.

questions.prompt: How does ElGamal encryption differ from textbook RSA?
options: ElGamal is non-deterministic (probabilistic) using an ephemeral random k per message
ElGamal produces shorter ciphertexts than plaintexts
questions.explanation: ElGamal incorporates a fresh random number k into every encryption, so encrypting 'SECRET' ten times produces ten totally different ciphertexts.
wrongExplanations: Correct! Randomized encryption prevents codebook eavesdropping attacks.
ElGamal is based on cyclic group mathematics.
ElGamal is an asymmetric public-key system.
ElGamal ciphertext consists of two group elements (c1, c2), doubling length.
questions.realWorldExample: ElGamal encryption is the direct ancestor of the US Digital Signature Algorithm (DSA).

questions.prompt: If Alice's public key is A, and Bob's private key is b, how does Bob compute the shared secret K?
questions.explanation: Bob raises Alice's public key A to his own private key b: K = (g^a)^b = g^(ab) mod p.
wrongExplanations: Correct! K = A^b mod p.
Addition does not yield the shared secret exponent.
Multiplication does not match Diffie-Hellman mathematics.
Subtraction is invalid.
questions.realWorldExample: Both Alice (B^a mod p) and Bob (A^b mod p) arrive at the exact same key K = g^(ab) mod p.

ashRecap: Diffie-Hellman lets two strangers agree on a secret key in public. Always pair it with digital certificates so an eavesdropper can't stand in the middle!
